question: Can you provide the originating cast_id (or exact station plus UTC datetime) for each DIC sample?
context: Only 24.7% of DIC rows currently match a bottle cast via site_key + datetime (±3 d); a provider-supplied cast/bottle id or precise datetime would raise the match rate (issue #47). UPDATE 2026-10-04 (WS-1004X2): the 3,254 samples that match no cast and have a source depth are now published as observations on their own calcofi_dic:bottle:<md5> keys with NO cast foreign key (parent_sample_key NULL): these values are not linked to a bottle cast, and a consumer must not join them to one. Some may be Niskins of casts already in the bottle database whose date the file gives only to the month (not verified). A provider cast/bottle id would let them dedup onto the bottle samples as the 1,065 matched rows already do (1,074 at v2026.10.01: two casts of 106.7 100.0 on 1984-01-19 tie for the same DIC rows). Separately, 38 of the 1,086 cast-matched DIC rows (EXPOCODEs 31JD19840711 and 31JD19841002, ship JD) sit on a bottle cast of another ship's cruise (1984-07-32NM, 1984-10-32NM): the +/-3 d site match crossed cruises.

label: Q07
question: Every DIC bottle that shares no Niskin with the bottle database reaches the release with no cruise_key (3,255 of 3,262 DIC samples; 1,926 of their datetimes sit on the 1st of the month). Is EXPOCODE (NODC ship code + cruise start date) the intended cruise designation for every row, including those a Niskin match never found?
context: At v2026.10.01 cruise_key was projected only through the matched bottle cast; the unmatched majority carried none, so the cruise_key integrity gate holds them in a ratchet (CRUISE_KEY_NULL_MAX dic = 3255). UPDATE 2026-10-04 (WS-1004X): grid_key is no longer taken from the matched cast alone; the ingest assigns it from each sample's own position (assign_grid_key), so all 3,261 minted samples carry one (the 6 cast-matched keep their cast's key). UPDATE 2026-10-04 (WS-1004X2, Ben: publish wherever the source gives a depth): the 3,255 samples that match no cast (the 3,262 above was a miscount; 3,261 samples are minted, 6 on a matched cast) now also carry a cruise_key where the SWFSC reference resolves one from the sample's ship (EXPOCODE NODC prefix, else Ship_Name) and date: 2,920 keyed (span containment or the event's month, cruise_key_method), 335 NULL on 8 EXPOCODEs for which the ingest's cruise reference holds no cruise of that ship and month (Sally Ride 240 samples, McArthur 51, Oceanus 41, David Starr Jordan 3). The EXPOCODE's start month is deliberately NOT passed as the designation: it differs from the span-resolved cruise's month in 545 of the 1,971 rows the span alone resolves (a cruise starting 28 Jan is designated February), so this question stays open. Their observations are now published too, on each sample's own key and with no cast link, wherever the source gives a depth: 12,681 values on 3,254 samples (alkalinity 3,126, ctdtemp_its90 3,174, dic 3,208, salinity_pss78 3,173). One sample has no source depth (Depth = -999) and stays a sample row with no observations: expocode 33RL20210116, station 080.0 090.0, 2021-01-20 (DIC 2007.2 and TA 2208.4 umol/kg left out). Of the 3,254 published samples, 3,218 carry a date on the 1st (1,926) or the 20th (1,292) of a month: an apparent month-precision stand-in (see Q02), not a sampling day.
proposed_answer: Derive ship_key from the EXPOCODE's NODC prefix and resolve cruise_key against the SWFSC cruise reference by the EXPOCODE start date (calcofi4db::resolve_cruise_key, span first, then the expocode month), so every DIC row carries the cruise its provider designated; the row's own month-precision datetime is not used for the match.
